title.narrative: Output 2.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to engage in a forward-looking international labour standards policy

description.narrative: The Baluchistan Provincial Tripartite Consultative Committee (PTCC) held intensive consultations in 2020-2021 to meet new emerging requirements to adopt new labour laws and related Rules of Business. Numerous consultations and rigorous discussions on the draft laws resulted in the promulgation of the following laws in 2021: Balochistan Factory Act, Shops and Establishments Act, Payments of Wages Act, Minimum Wages Act, Employment of Children (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Act and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act. Tripartite consultations were also organized on related draft Baluchistan Rules of Business in 2021. Tripartite consultations significantly intensified at and /or within the framework of the Federal Tripartite Consultative Committee (FTCC) in 2018-2021. In-depth discussions examined 41 ILO newly adopted instruments pending for submission to the competent authority (Parliament of Pakistan) since 1994. As a result, instruments were submitted to Parliament in 2021 for its consideration. Based on these consultations along with considerations by the Federal Cabinet the Pakistan Government requested ILO to support gap analyses of nine ILS. Tripartite consultations, including with relevant stakeholders beyond the FTCC, such as representatives of the maritime sector and domestic workers, were organized to discuss gap analyses reports on C.183 and MLC, 2006 in 2020, and on C.189, C.149, C.121, C.175 and P.29 in 2021; several tripartite consultations on C.176 took place 2017-2021, while the final draft of the C.102 gap analysis will be subject to tripartite consultations in 2022-2023. As a result, the ratifications of C.176 and the MLC, 2006 were supported by the tripartite constituents at the consultation stage. The Office provided technical support through the EU-funded DG-Trade and DG-DEVCO projects in 2016-2020 and the Trade for Decent Work (T4DW) in 2021. It also supported the development of the drafts and facilitated comments from tripartite constituents, the organisation of tripartite consultations, as well as the discussions and meetings of the Baluchistan PTCC. Moreover, the ILO supported the organisation of tripartite consultations, including at the FTCC, on the submission of pending newly adopted instruments to the competent authority, through the EU-funded ILES project and on gap analyses reports on C.183, C.189, C.176, C.149, C.121, C.175, C.102, P.29 and the MLC, 2006, through the above-mentioned projects, the Dutch-funded SLISP Project and the GIZ-funded project on the Baldia Arrangement, the OECD-WHO-ILO Work for Health partnership.

description.narrative:
The CEACR in 2020 and 2021 observations noted with satisfaction that section 3(2) of the Sindh Prohibition of Employment of Children Act 2017, prohibits the employment of adolescents in 38 hazardous occupations and activities listed in its schedule. The Committee further notes the Government’s indication that the Balochistan Employment of Children (Prohibition and Regulation) Bill, 2019 has also updated the list of hazardous occupations and processes prohibited to young persons and the ICT administration is in the process of adopting laws prohibiting hazardous types of work by young persons under the age of 18 years.
ILO provided technical assistance to the Government of Pakistan and social partners and supported strengthening of a culture of tripartite social dialogue on ILS, its application, and the associated reporting. The ILO used multiple strategies to strengthen social dialogue, including training for constituents, supporting the convening and facilitation of social dialogue fora both PTCC, FTCC, and purpose-oriented meetings. The timely submission of reports to the ILO Supervisory Mechanisms clearly demonstrates the overall improvement in national capacity to apply ILS in law reforms, judicial processes, and other relevant fields and report well on time.
